newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up slightly vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up slightly vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly at 8.3006 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday from Monday's 8.3010 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, on a report of higher foreign exchange reserves.

The yuan opened unchanged at 8.3010 and consolidated around that level, hitting an intra-day low of 8.3012. It then rose above 8.3000, reaching a high of 8.2997 before falling back late in the session.
The main bullish factor was a newspaper report quoting central bank governor Dai Xianglong as saying China's foreign exchange reserves had reached $98 billion, traders said.
This will reduce demand for foreign exchange, they said.
Trading was more active than on Monday, with most done at 8.3005, traders said.

Dealers said lower intervention by the central bank encouraged buying of yuan but it was firmly capped at the 8.30 level. "The yuan breached the key 8.30 resistance but failed to stay firm above that level," said one dealer.
Dealers expect the yuan to move in a narrow range of 8.3000 and 8.3010 on Wednesday.
The yuan continued its uptrend against 100 Japanese yen to close at 7.2475 from 7.3005 because of the fall of the yen in world markets.
The yuan ended at an intra-day high of 1.0727 from 1.0733 against the Hong Kong dollar.
